selection_policy: Small default positive corpus of public repositories with clear onboarding, focused APIs, readable tests, documented intent, and explicit boundaries; negative and mixed repositories are held out for evals rather than used as runtime taste anchors. Entries pin reviewed refs so evidence anchors are stable. Users may override this corpus.

repos.why_included: A mature Python CLI library with a small public surface, clear usage examples, and documentation that teaches the mental model before advanced features.
taste_signals: Public API is centered on a few composable decorators and command objects.
Documentation starts with simple examples before exposing advanced behavior.
Tests exercise user-visible CLI behavior instead of only internals.

evidence_anchors.why: Shows the value proposition and quickest copyable command pattern for newcomers.
Demonstrates how Click teaches decorators, commands, and options incrementally.
Provides concrete examples of testing user-visible CLI behavior.

repos.taste_boundary: Use Click as a benchmark for decorator-driven CLI ergonomics and progressive disclosure; do not reward hidden command magic unless the user path stays obvious.

repos.why_included: A Python HTTP client with a familiar interface, strong docs, and clear separation between public client APIs and transport internals.
taste_signals: Common usage is obvious from the top-level API.
Advanced transport behavior is isolated behind explicit boundaries.
Docs and tests explain both synchronous and asynchronous use cases.

evidence_anchors.why: Introduces the requests-like mental model and the public client surface.
Shows the expected path from simple requests to clients, streaming, and async usage.
Marks the internal transport seam that keeps advanced behavior out of the common path.

repos.taste_boundary: Use HTTPX as a benchmark for familiar HTTP ergonomics with explicit sync, async, and transport boundaries; penalize designs that hide lifecycle or transport complexity in the top-level API.

repos.why_included: A CLI framework optimized for user ergonomics with examples that make the intended path easy to copy and adapt.
taste_signals: Simple programs require little boilerplate.
Type hints serve both implementation and user-facing behavior.
Examples make the library feel usable before reading internals.

evidence_anchors.why: Frames the no-boilerplate promise and shows the smallest useful CLI shape.
Captures the intended learning path from Python function signatures to CLI behavior.
Shows where the framework explains option defaults, help text, and validation.

repos.taste_boundary: Use Typer as a benchmark for developer-experience-first CLIs where annotations reduce ceremony; penalize clever type usage when it makes command behavior harder to predict.

repos.why_included: A compact educational codebase where the architecture is intentionally small enough to understand in one sitting.
taste_signals: Core concepts map directly to small, readable code units.
The project avoids unnecessary abstraction for its stated purpose.
Tests and examples reinforce the main mental model.

evidence_anchors.why: Explains the educational scope and sets expectations for a tiny implementation.
Contains the compact core abstraction that carries the project mental model.
Shows the intended behavior through small examples instead of framework-heavy tests.

repos.taste_boundary: Use micrograd as a benchmark for pedagogical minimalism and conceptual compression; do not treat missing production concerns as taste failures inside its educational scope.

repos.why_included: A compact GPT training codebase that makes transformer model definition, training, configuration, and sampling approachable without a production framework stack.
taste_signals: Core training and model logic are concentrated in small, readable files.
The README gives copyable quick-start paths for both tiny local experiments and larger GPT-2 reproduction.
Configuration files expose the important model and training choices without hiding them behind a framework.

evidence_anchors.why: Explains the simple training path, intended scope, dependencies, and why the repo is deliberately compact.
Contains the focused GPT model definition that keeps the main mental model visible.
Shows the training loop and operational choices without scattering them across a large framework.
Provides a small, copyable local experiment path that helps newcomers build intuition.

repos.taste_boundary: Use nanoGPT as a benchmark for educational ML/AI hackability and transparent training loops; do not treat omitted production deployment, safety, or large-scale orchestration concerns as failures inside its learning-oriented scope.

repos.why_included: A mature ML library with a famously consistent estimator API, extensive examples, strong contributor guidance, and tests that enforce cross-estimator behavior.
taste_signals: The estimator interface makes diverse models feel predictable through shared fit, predict, transform, and parameter conventions.
Developer documentation explains API contracts and contribution expectations rather than leaving conventions implicit.
Common tests and examples reinforce consistency across a large model surface.

evidence_anchors.why: Frames the project scope, installation path, contributor guide, and documentation entry points.
Documents estimator API conventions and expectations for compatible components.
Shows the shared estimator base behavior that anchors the library's public mental model.
Captures common estimator behavior through executable cross-library checks.

repos.taste_boundary: Use scikit-learn as a benchmark for large ML library API consistency and contributor-facing contracts; do not require small experimental repos to copy its full compatibility and test matrix.

repos.why_included: A modern LLM framework that treats language-model calls as typed program modules, with explicit seams between signatures, prediction modules, and prompt/program optimization.
taste_signals: Signatures make LLM inputs and outputs explicit instead of burying contracts in prose prompts.
Prediction modules compose behavior such as chain-of-thought by extending signatures rather than scattering prompt strings across call sites.
Optimization machinery is separated from the common declaration and execution path.

evidence_anchors.why: Shows the public surface and deliberate user-facing aliases.
Contains the core typed signature abstraction for declaring LLM input and output contracts.
Demonstrates a small composition layer that adds reasoning by extending a signature and wrapping Predict.
Exercises user-facing signature behavior with compact examples.

repos.taste_boundary: Use DSPy as a benchmark for declarative LLM I/O contracts and separating program structure from prompt optimization; do not require simple prompt scripts to adopt Signature or optimizer machinery unless systematic prompt improvement is a project value.

repos.why_included: A large LLM-era model library that explicitly documents its scope, public mental model, and tradeoff between broad model coverage and per-model researcher iteration speed.
taste_signals: The public API gives users a stable task-oriented path before they need model internals.
Contributor documentation explains the one-folder-per-model pattern and why model files are not aggressively refactored into shared abstractions.
The project states when not to use the library, making scope boundaries explicit instead of implied.

evidence_anchors.why: Documents the public quickstart and explicit when-to-use/when-not-to-use scope boundary.
Explains model contribution conventions and the rationale for keeping model implementations self-contained.
Defines the preprocess, forward, and postprocess pipeline seam for task-oriented inference.
Provides runnable, task-scoped examples outside the core library internals.

repos.taste_boundary: Use Transformers as a benchmark for large ML library scope declarations, task-oriented pipeline APIs, and honest contributor documentation about architectural tradeoffs; do not use model count or internal model-file complexity as taste evidence by itself.

repos.why_included: A systems-level ML inference project with an explicit public C API boundary, hardware-aware layering, and examples that consume the API without leaking implementation internals.
taste_signals: The public header separates model-level inference contracts from tensor backend implementation details.
Examples use the public API as the application boundary, making lifecycle and resource management visible.
The architecture separates tensor primitives, model inference APIs, and application examples instead of mixing hardware concerns into user code.

evidence_anchors.why: Defines the public API contract and visibility boundary for consumers.
Explains quickstart commands, supported backends, quantization, and GGUF at the user level.
Shows standalone consumers using the public API for common inference workflows.
Shows implementation concerns split below the public header boundary.

repos.taste_boundary: Use llama.cpp as a benchmark for C-level ML inference API design, explicit public-header contracts, and hardware-aware layering; do not apply its native optimization constraints to Python ML libraries or simple LLM applications.

repos.why_included: A Rust search tool that balances a fast default path, practical CLI ergonomics, and detailed documentation for users who need to understand search behavior.
taste_signals: The default command path optimizes for the most common recursive search workflow.
Documentation explains performance, ignore rules, Unicode behavior, and edge cases without hiding tradeoffs.
The project exposes powerful options while keeping the first-run mental model small.

evidence_anchors.why: Introduces the tool, its defaults, and the user-facing reasons it feels faster and simpler.
Explains advanced search behavior and option tradeoffs while preserving the core mental model.

repos.taste_boundary: Use ripgrep as a benchmark for high-performance CLI taste where complexity earns its keep by improving search UX, defaults, and cross-platform behavior.

repos.why_included: A Go HTTP router that stays close to net/http, uses small composable interfaces, and teaches middleware and routing through compact examples.
taste_signals: The API composes handlers, routers, and middleware without requiring a full application framework.
Examples demonstrate practical routing patterns before readers need to inspect internals.
The project keeps extension points idiomatic to Go's standard HTTP model.

evidence_anchors.why: Shows the router contract, middleware model, and concise examples for common HTTP services.
Provides runnable reference patterns that calibrate what the project considers idiomatic use.

repos.taste_boundary: Use chi as a benchmark for composable Go HTTP routing that avoids framework sprawl; penalize designs that bury net/http semantics behind unnecessary abstraction.

repos.why_included: A compact embedded database with unusually strong correctness culture, source-tree documentation, portability discipline, and explicit testing practices.
taste_signals: The source tree documents how the project is built, tested, and organized.
Correctness work includes multiple test harnesses, fuzzing, crash/OOM/I/O cases, and release checklists.
The architecture earns its complexity through portability and reliability constraints.

evidence_anchors.why: Maps the source tree and build/test workflow for contributors.
Shows the breadth of behavior, failure-mode, and regression testing.
Explains the parallel test runner, release-test workflow, failure investigation path, and observable test outputs.

repos.taste_boundary: Use SQLite as a benchmark for correctness-heavy systems where deep tests and portability matter; do not require small apps to copy database-grade release machinery.

repos.why_included: A systems codebase often praised for understandable C, direct data-structure implementation, and a simple user-facing product model.
taste_signals: The operational model is easy to explain before reading internals.
Core implementation choices stay close to the product's data-structure concepts.
Documentation and command references keep user-facing behavior concrete.

evidence_anchors.why: Explains quick start, build path, command model, and project scope.
Contains the direct C implementation of server behavior and data structures.
Shows executable coverage of user-visible command behavior.

repos.taste_boundary: Use Redis as a benchmark for direct systems design and product simplicity; treat it as a code and product-design reference, not an endorsement of current project governance or licensing, and do not over-reward global state or single-process assumptions outside this domain.

repos.why_included: A Python library that exposes a compact type-driven public model while hiding substantial validation and migration complexity.
taste_signals: The public API lets users express validation through canonical Python type hints.
Docs and migration guides acknowledge compatibility pressure instead of hiding it.
Developer experience is a first-class design value rather than an afterthought.

evidence_anchors.why: Frames the type-hint mental model and shows the smallest useful model shape.
Shows the public learning path, concepts, and migration guidance.
Captures validation behavior across many input and compatibility cases.

repos.taste_boundary: Use Pydantic as a benchmark for type-driven user APIs; do not assume validation frameworks are appropriate when a plain data structure would encode the invariant better.

repos.why_included: A documentation-rich Python library where examples, API affordances, and visual output ergonomics make the common path approachable.
taste_signals: The README shows concrete output examples before advanced configuration.
API surfaces are designed around user intent such as tables, progress, logging, and pretty output.
Documentation treats examples and screenshots as part of the interface contract.

evidence_anchors.why: Demonstrates install/run commands, examples, and visual API affordances.
Shows the guided learning path for common terminal UI tasks.
Grounds visual and formatting behavior in executable expectations.

repos.taste_boundary: Use Rich as a benchmark for user-facing API empathy and example quality; do not apply visual-output priorities to non-UI libraries without an inferred value fit.

repos.why_included: A small Ruby testing library that calibrates pragmatic minimalism, low ceremony, and practical interfaces over speculative abstraction.
taste_signals: The project stays small enough for users to understand the testing model quickly.
Public APIs favor practical test writing over framework ceremony.
Metaprogramming earns its keep by reducing user friction without hiding the core model.

evidence_anchors.why: Explains the small-library philosophy and primary user-facing API.
Shows the compact implementation of assertions, specs, and test execution.
Shows the library testing itself through its own usage patterns.

repos.taste_boundary: Use Minitest as a benchmark for low-ceremony library design; do not treat minimalism as a reason to omit explicit safety checks in high-risk domains.
